caseStudy.title: Nexus Platform Redesign
caseStudy.problem: Client-side rendering was heavily taxing user hardware, and synchronous API chains created fragile dependency bottlenecks that frequently cascaded into full application outages.
caseStudy.overview: Nexus is an enterprise data visualization platform utilized by Fortune 500 logistics teams. The legacy monolith was struggling under immense technical debt, leading to excruciatingly slow query times and UI freezes during peak load.
caseStudy.subtitle: Re-architecting an enterprise logistics data visualizer for 10x throughput.

decisions.answer: Hybrid rendering requirements: Static site generation for public marketing pages and server-side streaming for live data dashboards to achieve optimal SEO and sub-100ms load times.
decisions.question: Why Next.js App Router?

decisions.answer: Eliminated infrastructure management overhead while retaining fine-grained autoscaling triggers during peak traffic periods.
decisions.question: Why AWS ECS Fargate?

keyChallenges.title: Real-time State Synchronization
keyChallenges.description: Maintaining state parity across thousands of concurrent client dashboards required moving away from polling to a Redis Pub/Sub WebSocket engine.

keyChallenges.title: Zero Layout Shift & Micro-Bundle Splitting
keyChallenges.description: Implemented route-level dynamic code splitting and React Server Components to stream data directly into the DOM, eliminating spinners and layout shifts.

problemPoints: > P99 response times exceeding 4,500ms under load
> DOM node count exceeding 15,000 elements on primary views
> Tightly coupled state leading to memory leaks and memory spikes
caseStudy.myRoleDescription: As Lead Engineer, directed a team of five engineers through a full-stack re-architecture. Responsibilities included designing the event-driven GraphQL backend, implementing Next.js Server Components rendering patterns, and defining strict CI/CD zero-downtime deployments.

caseStudy.myRoleDescription: Directed full-stack engineering team through system migration.

experience.description: Led the architectural redesign of the core data processing engine, reducing P99 latency by 42%. Managed a cross-functional team of 6 engineers across full-stack deliverables and real-time dashboard telemetry.

caseStudy.title: Vertex High-Frequency Trading Terminal
caseStudy.problem: Traditional DOM rendering froze browser threads when receiving over 1,000 ticker updates per second.
caseStudy.overview: Vertex Financial required an ultra-low latency trading interface capable of visualizing live stock order books and algorithmic trade executions without drop in frame rate.
caseStudy.subtitle: Real-time financial telemetry dashboard rendering 50,000+ data nodes.

decisions.answer: DOM SVG nodes overhead scaled exponentially beyond 5,000 elements, whereas WebGL instanced rendering maintained 60 FPS for 50,000+ data nodes.
decisions.question: Why WebGL over SVG?

keyChallenges.title: Offscreen Canvas & Web Workers
keyChallenges.description: Offloaded WebGL buffer generation to background Web Workers to maintain 60 FPS UI responsiveness.

problemPoints: > Frame rates dropping below 15 FPS during market volatility
> Memory leak build-up over 8-hour trading sessions
> Canvas re-render queue blocking UI input events
caseStudy.myRoleDescription: Designed custom WebGL instanced rendering pipelines and worker threads for parsing incoming WebSocket binary protocols.

experience.description: Developed a high-frequency trading dashboard with real-time WebGL charting. Improved client rendering performance for datasets exceeding 50,000 active nodes without UI lag.

caseStudy.title: Acme Component Engine & Micro-Frontends
caseStudy.problem: Duplicate component implementations caused inconsistent branding, bundle bloat, and slow release cycles.
caseStudy.overview: Unified fragmented product codebases into a shared, accessible component design system and automated CI/CD pipeline.
caseStudy.subtitle: Modular frontend design system scaling across 5 enterprise product lines.

decisions.answer: Allowed independent team deployments while maintaining strict brand consistency and 40% smaller bundle sizes.
decisions.question: Why Modular Component Architecture?

keyChallenges.title: Tree-Shaking & Bundle Minimization
keyChallenges.description: Optimized ES module exports to allow lazy-loading of UI components on demand.

problemPoints: > Bundle size exceeding 3.5 MB per initial page load
> Inconsistent UI patterns across product lines
caseStudy.myRoleDescription: Built core design tokens, automated accessibility test suites, and managed npm package distribution across engineering teams.

experience.description: Architected modern microservices and modular UI design systems used across 5 flagship product lines. Reduced bundle sizes by 40% and improved TTI by 1.2s.

about.title: Curious by Default.
about.paragraph1: Software engineering is not just a technical discipline; it is a craft. The internal architecture behind a system should be as clean, robust, and intentional as the interface the user interacts with.
about.paragraph2: My approach is rooted in pragmatism, performance metrics, and zero-compromise code safety. I write code designed for maintainability, enforce rigorous automated testing, and continuously optimize for low end-user latency.
